title: Grateful Dead Live at Harpur College on 1970-05-02
lineage: Dat (Sony PCM-R500) > Sound Devices 744T > Adobe Audition CC 2015 >Samplitude Pro X3 Suite > FLAC/

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard recording of a sublime 1970 marathon with an acoustic opener, NRPS interlude and electric sets highlighted by a smoking Friend of the Devil and The Other One.
ai_review.review: Fans rave that the Miller‑sourced soundboard is “gorgeous,” “like being in the room,” and balanced enough to capture every nuance of the acoustic set and the two electric marathons.  The show itself is praised as a classic four‑set experience – acoustic gems (Friend of the Devil, Dire Wolf, Cumberland Blues) flow into an NRPS set and then fire‑up with a sublime Other One suite, Cosmic Charlie and Viola Lee.  A few reviewers note minor tape quirks and a sub‑par Cold Rain & Snow, but the overall consensus is that this recording delivers both historic value and musical bliss.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive fan comments on both performance and soundboard quality; only a handful of mixed/negative notes, giving an overall rating well above the average star score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the audio as crisp, balanced and “like being in the room,” with no major drop‑outs. Minor complaints involve set‑list labeling and tiny reel‑flip gaps, but none affect overall clarity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A relaxed acoustic opening (with a brief NRPS set) gives way to two powerful electric sets and a concise encore, delivering a varied yet cohesive 1970‑era experience that fans describe as cosmic, funky and “over the mountain.”

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his soaring guitar tone (“over the mountain”) and leadership of the electric set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted on amplified bass during Cumberland Blues; otherwise not singled out.
